newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Thames to seek buyback mandate.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Thames to seek buyback mandate.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Thames Water Plc will seek a mandate from shareholders at its annual meeting for a buyback of shares, managing director Bill Alexander told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"We are applying to the AGM for a mandate," he said, after the company set up its first share buyback of 10 percent last year.
Thames said year pretax profits before exceptional items rose 19 percent to 384 million stg and paid out a total dividend of 34.4 pence, up 22 percent, aided by the reduction of shares in issue.

The company said in a statement with results that it intended to maintain real dividend growth and Alexander said that although payouts were unlikely to match 22 percent, "we'll be paying a reasonable dividend going forward."
"It'll not be 22 percent again unless of course we have another share buyback," he said.

The company said that its ability to increase the dividend was also a result of a strong contribution from non-regulated business including international operations, which contributed 26 million stg to profits and should see a strengthening earnings stream.
"We'd like to be able to attribute about 10 percent of our profits to our non-core activities...by the year 2000," Alexander said.
He said the company was not looking for any acquisitions at this stage, but "what we're doing is looking at growing our international business...that's the way we're going forward."
